nē … quidem

adverbs, with the stressed word between them

not even; not … either

The word that is stressed stands between nē and quidem: nē jocō quidem, not even as a joke. It also gives “not … either”: nē ego quidem, nor do I. After nōn modo, “not only not … but not even”: nōn modo … sed nē … quidem.

Examples

  • Amīcum laedere nē jocō quidem licet.

    You may not hurt a friend, not even as a joke.Ps.-Publ. A 23

  • vidēmus igitur ut conquiēscere nē īnfantēs quidem possint

    so we see that not even babies can keep stillCic. Fin. 5.55

  • nē exspectēmus quidem, dum rogēmur; studium semper adsit, cūnctātiō absit

    let us not even wait to be asked; let eagerness always be there, and hesitation neverCic. Amic. 44

  • nōn assuēscat ergō, nē dum īnfāns quidem est, sermōnī quī dēdiscendus sit

    so let him not get used, not even while he is a baby, to speech he will have to unlearnQuint. 1.1.5

See also not, even, not only … but also.
